findings.claim: The line-oriented declares_workspace parser fails on valid TOML like `[ workspace ]` (with spaces) causing a false negative, and incorrectly matches `[workspace]` inside comments or multi-line strings causing a false positive.

Existing tests like test_changelog_missing still use temp_dir.path() directly as project_path. Its parent is the host's $TMPDIR. If the host has /tmp/Cargo.toml declaring a workspace and /tmp/CHANGELOG.md, the tests will still fail exactly as they did before.

The new behaviour correctly fixes the fallback to require a workspace root, but traversing up to the true workspace root (or reading package.workspace) would be a more robust fix for crates deeper than one level.
Ratchets have been maintained. unwrap_calls_src_total is 20336 and panic_calls_src_total is 785. The .pmat-ratchet.toml file is unchanged.

lanes.summary: do-not-implement-as-written. The `declares_workspace` predicate has a concrete failure on line 86: it fails to recognize valid TOML workspaces with trailing comments (`[workspace] # comment`) or spaces (`[ workspace ]`), which wrongly deflates scores. It also falsely matches `[workspace]` inside multi-line strings, which wrongly inflates scores. Furthermore, the problem was moved rather than fully fixed for the older tests (like `test_changelog_missing`): because their project root is directly in `$TMPDIR`, they will still fail if the host has BOTH `/tmp/Cargo.toml` (with a workspace) and `/tmp/CHANGELOG.md`.

findings.claim: Concrete failure for Q1: `declares_workspace()` uses `line.trim() == "[workspace]"` which evaluates to false if the line has a trailing comment (e.g. `[workspace] # comment`) or spaces (e.g. `[ workspace ]`). This produces a WRONG score by deflating it (fails to recognize a valid workspace parent, dropping the score). Conversely, `[workspace]` inside a multi-line string will falsely match, incorrectly inflating the score.

For Q2: The old code only checked exactly `project_path.parent()`, so a crate 2 levels down NEVER got the right fallback anyway. Losing it is not worse than the bug. Walking to the real root is a better fix, but out of scope for this hermeticity bugfix.

For Q3: The 4 new tests are high quality. Test 1 & 2 genuinely fail on old code, the control test genuinely fails if the feature is deleted, and they do not leave state behind or depend on environment because they use a nested `proj/` directory inside the `TempDir`.

For Q4: The fix MOVED the problem for the older tests (like `test_changelog_missing`). Those older tests still use `temp_dir.path()` as the project root, meaning their parent is `$TMPDIR`. If the host filesystem happens to have BOTH `/tmp/Cargo.toml` (declaring a workspace) AND `/tmp/CHANGELOG.md`, those old tests will STILL fail.
For Q5 (Ratchets): Measured `unwrap()` calls at exactly 20336 and `panic!(` calls at exactly 785. The `.pmat-ratchet.toml` file was unmodified, meaning no baselines were changed.
